questions.text: Which of the following compounds exhibits hydrogen bonding?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Hydrogen bonding occurs only when H is bonded to N, O, or F. Among the options, only NH₃ has N–H bonds. Step-by-step: CH₄ has C–H (C not electronegative enough), HCl has H–Cl (Cl less electronegative than N/O/F), CO₂ has no hydrogen. Hence NH₃ shows hydrogen bonding.

questions.text: Select the missing term from the given alternatives: Z, X, V, T, R, ?, N
questions.solution: Shortcut: Note the reverse alphabetical positions (Z=26, X=24, V=22...). The value decreases by 2 each step; the missing value is 16, corresponding to P. Full Solution: The series follows a pattern of skipping one letter in reverse alphabetical order. Z (skip Y) → X (skip W) → V (skip U) → T (skip S) → R (skip Q) → P (skip O) → N. Therefore, the missing term is P.

questions.text: As per the Constitution of India, what is the total number of Schedules currently in force?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use Option Elimination via Amendment tracking. Original Constitution had 8 Schedules. Four major amendments added one Schedule each: 9th (1st Amend), 10th (52nd Amend), 11th (73rd Amend), 12th (74th Amend). 8 + 4 = 12. Eliminate 10, 11, 13. Full Solution: The Indian Constitution originally contained 8 Schedules. The 9th Schedule was added by the 1st Amendment Act, 1951 (Land Reforms). The 10th Schedule was added by the 52nd Amendment Act, 1985 (Anti-Defection Law). The 11th Schedule was added by the 73rd Amendment Act, 1992 (Panchayats). The 12th Schedule was added by the 74th Amendment Act, 1992 (Municipalities). No further Schedules have been added, making the current total 12.

questions.text: What is the elevation of Kanchenjunga, the highest mountain peak located entirely within India?
questions.solution: Shortcut: K2 (8,611 m) is in PoK, not fully in India. Kanchenjunga is the 3rd highest globally. Remember the unit digit '6' for Kanchenjunga (8586). Step-by-step: Mount Everest (8,848 m) is in Nepal/China. K2 (8,611 m) lies in Gilgit-Baltistan (PoK). Kanchenjunga (8,586 m) lies on the Sikkim-Nepal border, making it the highest peak entirely within Indian territory. Option A matches the verified elevation.

questions.text: If \( x + \frac{1}{x} = 4 \), what is the value of \( x^3 + \frac{1}{x^3} \)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use the identity \( (x + \frac{1}{x})^3 = x^3 + \frac{1}{x^3} + 3(x + \frac{1}{x}) \). Substitute the given value: \( 4^3 = x^3 + \frac{1}{x^3} + 3(4) \Rightarrow 64 = x^3 + \frac{1}{x^3} + 12 \Rightarrow x^3 + \frac{1}{x^3} = 52 \). Step-by-step: Cube both sides of the given equation \( x + \frac{1}{x} = 4 \). The expansion of \( (a+b)^3 \) is \( a^3 + b^3 + 3ab(a+b) \). Here \( a=x, b=\frac{1}{x} \), so \( ab=1 \). Thus \( (x + \frac{1}{x})^3 = x^3 + \frac{1}{x^3} + 3(1)(x + \frac{1}{x}) \). Substitute \( x + \frac{1}{x} = 4 \): \( 64 = x^3 + \frac{1}{x^3} + 12 \). Solving gives \( x^3 + \frac{1}{x^3} = 52 \).

questions.text: The difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest on a certain sum for 2 years at 10% per annum is ₹50. Find the principal sum.
questions.solution: Shortcut: For 2 years, Difference (CI - SI) = P * (R/100)^2. Here, 50 = P * (10/100)^2 = P/100. Therefore, P = 50 * 100 = ₹5,000. Worked: SI for 2 years = P * 10 * 2 / 100 = 0.2P. Amount in CI = P(1 + 10/100)^2 = 1.21P. CI = 0.21P. Difference = 0.21P - 0.2P = 0.01P = 50. Hence, P = 50 / 0.01 = ₹5,000.

questions.text: A shopkeeper marks an article 40% above its cost price and allows two successive discounts of 20% and 10% respectively. What is his profit or loss percentage?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Equivalent single discount for successive discounts of a% and b% is (a + b - ab/100)%. Here, equivalent discount = 20 + 10 - (20*10/100) = 28%. If CP = 100, MP = 140. SP = 140 * (100-28)/100 = 140 * 0.72 = 100.8. Profit % = 0.8%. Worked: Let CP = ₹100. MP = ₹140. After 20% discount, price = ₹112. After 10% discount, SP = ₹100.80. Profit = ₹0.80 on ₹100 = 0.8%.

questions.text: Which Fundamental Right was removed from Part III of the Constitution by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978 and subsequently made a legal right under Article 300A?
questions.solution: Shortcut (Option Elimination): The 44th Amendment is famous for reversing the 42nd Amendment's excesses. Options A, B, and D (Equality, Freedom, Remedies) form the 'Golden Triangle' (Articles 14, 19, 21/32) – the basic structure of the Constitution – and can never be removed. Only 'Right to Property' (formerly Art 31) was demoted to a legal right (Art 300A). Step-by-step: 1. Identify the 44th Amendment (1978) context: enacted by Janata Govt to restore constitutional sanity. 2. Recall Art 31 (Right to Property) was a major hurdle for land reforms. 3. The Amendment deleted Art 19(1)(f) and Art 31. 4. Inserted Art 300A: 'No person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law'. 5. Verify others: Art 14-18 (Equality), Art 19-22 (Freedom), Art 32 (Remedies) remain intact as Fundamental Rights.

questions.text: As of January 2024, what is the total number of Constitutional Amendment Acts enacted in India?
questions.solution: Shortcut: The 105th Amendment (2021) restored state powers for OBC lists; the 106th Amendment (Sept 2023) provided 33% women's reservation. No further amendment was enacted by Jan 2024. Step-by-step: The 104th Amendment (2020) extended SC/ST reservation. The 105th came in Aug 2021. The 106th (Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam) received assent in Sept 2023. Hence, the count stands at 106.

questions.text: Which Article of the Indian Constitution is described as the 'Heart and Soul of the Constitution' by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Associate 'Remedy' with 'Heart/Soul' — Article 32 provides the Right to Constitutional Remedies (writs), making other rights enforceable. Step-by-step: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar explicitly stated Article 32 is the most important article; it empowers citizens to move the Supreme Court directly for enforcement of Fundamental Rights via writs (Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, etc.). Article 19 covers Freedoms, Article 21 covers Life & Liberty, Article 14 covers Equality.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'CAT' is written as 'DBU'. How is 'DOG' written in that code?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Each letter is shifted one place forward in the alphabet (Caesar cipher +1). C→D, A→B, T→U, so DOG→E P H. Full solution: Write alphabet positions, add 1 to each, convert back: D(4)+1=5→E, O(15)+1=16→P, G(7)+1=8→H. Hence code is EPH.

questions.text: A man walks 10 km North, turns right and walks 5 km, turns right again and walks 10 km, then turns left and walks 10 km. What is the straight-line distance from his starting point?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Track Net Displacement. North-South: +10 (N) -10 (S) = 0. East-West: +5 (E) +10 (E) = 15 km East. Distance = 15 km. Step-by-step: 1. Start (0,0). 2. North 10 -> (0,10). 3. Right (East) 5 -> (5,10). 4. Right (South) 10 -> (5,0). 5. Left (East) 10 -> (15,0). Distance from origin = 15 km.

questions.text: An object is placed at a distance of 30 cm from a convex lens of focal length 20 cm. What is the nature and position of the image formed?

options.label: A
options.text: Real, Inverted, 60 cm on the other side of the lens

options.label: B
options.text: Virtual, Erect, 60 cm on the same side of the lens

options.label: C
options.text: Real, Inverted, 12 cm on the other side of the lens

options.label: D
options.text: Virtual, Erect, 12 cm on the same side of the lens

questions.solution: Shortcut: Object distance (30 cm) lies between F (20 cm) and 2F (40 cm). For a convex lens, this always produces a Real, Inverted, Magnified image beyond 2F (v > 40 cm). Only option with v=60 cm fits. Step-by-step: Using lens formula 1/v - 1/u = 1/f with u = -30 cm, f = +20 cm. 1/v = 1/20 - 1/30 = 1/60 => v = +60 cm. Positive v confirms Real image on opposite side. Magnification m = v/u = -2 (Inverted, Magnified).

questions.text: The atomic number of an element is 16. Based on its electronic configuration, which of the following correctly identifies its group and period in the Modern Periodic Table?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Atomic number 16 → Electronic configuration = 2, 8, 6. Period = Number of shells = 3. Valence electrons = 6 → p-block element → Group = 10 + Valence electrons = 16. Step-by-step: Electrons fill K-shell (2), L-shell (8), M-shell (6). The presence of 3 shells places it in Period 3. With 6 valence electrons in the outermost shell, it belongs to Group 16 (VIA group) of the p-block.

questions.text: The sides of a triangle are in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5. If the perimeter of the triangle is 48 cm, what is its area (in \(\text{cm}^2\))?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Recognize 3:4:5 as a Pythagorean triplet (right-angled triangle). Let sides be \(3x, 4x, 5x\). Perimeter \(12x = 48 \Rightarrow x = 4\). Sides are 12 cm, 16 cm, 20 cm. Area = \(\frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2} \times 12 \times 16 = 96\). Step-by-step: Sum of ratio terms = 3+4+5 = 12. Value of one part = 48/12 = 4. Sides = 12, 16, 20. Check right angle: \(12^2 + 16^2 = 144 + 256 = 400 = 20^2\). Area = 0.5 * 12 * 16 = 96 \(\text{cm}^2\).
